notes.subject: dɔnniya-ko
notes.rationale: חידה (riddle) has no single fixed Bambara word; 'dɔnniya-ko' (a knowing-thing) is coined — native ear should confirm.

notes.subject: אחודה / חידה
notes.rationale: The verb 'I will propound' and the noun 'riddle' share the root חוד — the knot-tying picture is lost in Bambara.

notes.subject: הגד
notes.rationale: Hebrew doubles the verb (הגד תגידו, 'declare-declare'); Bambara renders one verb, losing the infinitive-absolute emphasis.

notes.subject: n bɛ dɔnniya-ko dɔ fo aw ye
notes.rationale: Shimshon directly summons his thirty companions to take up the riddle.

notes.subject: don wolonwula · mugan ni tan
notes.rationale: The verse stakes counted quantities: seven days, thirty linens, thirty changes of garments.

notes.subject: aw
notes.rationale: Direct address by Shimshon to the thirty companions.

translation: Shimshon (Samisoni) y'u ko: “N bɛ dɔnniya-ko dɔ fo aw ye sisan: ni aw bɛ se ka ⟨את⟩ a fɔn n ye don wolonwula kɔnɔ, munmisɛn donw na, ani ka a ɲini ka sɔrɔ, n bɛna aw di dɔki mugan ni tan ani bɔrɔ-wɛrɛ mugan ni tan.”

tokens.gloss: ani ka a ɲini ka sɔrɔ
